description_full: Keisei Electric Railway Co., Ltd. engages in the operation of railway and bus transportation in Japan. It operates through Transportation, Distribution, Real Estate, Leisure and Service, Construction, and Other segments. The company operates railways, buses, taxis, and other transportation services. It also sells products through retail and department stores. In addition, the company is involved in real estate leasing and sales, as well as brokering, managing, and renovating; operates hotels, restaurants, movie theaters, advertising agencies, and travel agencies; and undertake civil engineering and construction work. Further, it builds and maintains other facilities, including residential buildings; and engages in rail car maintenance and insurance agency businesses. As of March 31, 2026, the company operates 762 passenger cars and 91 stations. Keisei Electric Railway Co., Ltd. was incorporated in 1909 and is headquartered in Ichikawa, Japan.

financial_summary: KEISEI ELECTRIC RAILWAY CO is a mid-cap industrials business with a $3.0B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $260M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.86× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 9.9×.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
